# Company 073 — Secrets & Credential Rotation Autopilot

**Company ID:** `company:future:073`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:073`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-073-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no credential discovery against external systems, rotation, revocation or application configuration mutation.

## Business identity
Purpose: discover credential dependencies, track lifecycle and safely rotate/revoke API keys, passwords, OAuth credentials, certificates, SSH keys, tokens, webhook secrets, service accounts and machine/agent credentials.

## Product tree
Secret Inventory; Ownership Registry; Dependency Discovery; Expiration Monitor; Rotation Scheduler; Dual-Key/Overlap Rotation; Emergency Revocation; Certificate Renewal; OAuth Client Rotation; Database Credential Rotation; Cloud/Service Account Rotation; SSH Key Rotation; Webhook Secret Rotation; Agent Credential Lifecycle; Vault Integrations; Application Update Orchestrator; Verification/Rollback; Leak Response; Policy/Compliance; Audit; API/SDK; Enterprise/Private Deployment; Provider Packs.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree
Features: credential reference/type/provider/account, owner, consumers/dependencies, scopes, created/last-rotated/expires, rotation method, overlap window, new/old state, verification probes, rollback, compromise state, policy, evidence and revocation propagation.
Customers: software teams, enterprises, security/IT, MSPs, DevOps, agent platforms, SaaS vendors and regulated organizations.
Verticals: cloud, databases, SaaS APIs, payments, CI/CD, developer tooling, AI agents, internal services and infrastructure.

## Brain capability / architecture
Brain may map dependencies and propose safe rotation sequence. Secret values remain outside Brain/memory/logs. Deterministic orchestration owns rotate→update consumers→verify→revoke-old, with protected approval based on risk. Architecture: secret-reference inventory, dependency graph, provider adapters, rotation state machine, temporary overlap, verification probes, rollback, audit and break-glass path.

## Agent tree
Credential Inventory Agent; Dependency Mapper; Expiry Agent; Rotation Planner; Provider Adapter Agent; Application Update Coordinator; Verification Agent; Emergency Revocation Agent; Leak Response Agent; Audit/Policy Agent.

## Deterministic services
Secret refs/vault APIs; dependency graph; schedule; locks; provider-specific rotation primitives; dual-key windows; config update transactions; health probes; rollback; redaction; one-time protected authorization; audit.

## Workflow
Credential registered/discovered → map owners/consumers → classify risk/expiry → plan rotation order/overlap → protected authorization → create/rotate new credential via provider → update exact dependent systems → verify all consumers → revoke old credential → monitor → close evidence; on failure rollback/contain without exposing value.

## Integrations / API / data
Vaults, clouds, databases, SaaS APIs, OAuth providers, certificate authorities, CI/CD, hosting, Kubernetes, code/config systems, webhooks, agent runtimes and SIEM. Data contains references/metadata/dependencies/evidence, not secret plaintext.

## Monetization / distribution
Credentials/dependencies/providers, rotations, seats, enterprise/private, compliance packs, API and managed security. Distribution via cloud/security/DevOps ecosystems and MSPs.

## Security/privacy/compliance
Highest secret-handling standard: zero plaintext exposure to client/Brain/logs, ephemeral secret handling, strict least privilege, two-person/step-up where needed, break-glass audit, no automatic broad rotation when dependency completeness is uncertain.

## Failure / edge cases
Unknown consumer, provider only allows destructive rotation, dual-key unsupported, app update succeeds partially, rollback impossible, stale instance still uses old key, certificate chain issue, clock skew, secret leaked during transition, provider outage, emergency revocation breaks service. Dependency uncertainty must block routine destructive revocation.

## Scale / overlap
Small vault inventory → enterprise credential lifecycle → machine/agent credential control plane. Overlap #5 audit, #66 runtime security, #74 permissions, #91 agent identity. #073 owns credential lifecycle/rotation.

## Classification
**DESIGN NOW:** secret-reference-only architecture, dependency graph, rotation/version states, protected credential actions, redaction, audit/rollback.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center already needs P2.5 secret isolation; reverse-map confirms rotation/dependency metadata must be first-class.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** external vault/provider adapters and customer dependency discovery.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** commercial scanners/provider packs/pricing.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** global credential fleet and automated certificate/key infrastructure.

# Mandatory 24-part completion block
1. Product Tree: inventory/ownership/dependencies/expiry/scheduler/dual-key/revoke/certs/OAuth/DB/cloud/SSH/webhook/agent/vault/update/verify/leak/API.
2. Feature Tree: reference/type/provider/account/owner/consumers/scopes/dates/method/overlap/state/probes/rollback/compromise/evidence.
3. Customer Tree: software/enterprise/security/IT/MSP/DevOps/agents/SaaS/regulated.
4. Vertical Tree: cloud/DB/SaaS/payments/CI/devtools/AI/internal infra.
5. Brain Tree: dependency/sequence reasoning only; secret values prohibited.
6. Agent Tree: inventory/dependency/expiry/planner/provider/update/verifier/revocation/leak/audit.
7. Service Tree: vault refs/graph/scheduler/locks/rotation/config update/probes/rollback/redaction/auth/audit.
8. Workflow Tree: register→map→plan→authorize→rotate→update→verify→revoke→monitor/evidence.
9. Integration Tree: vault/cloud/DB/SaaS/OAuth/CA/CI/K8s/config/webhooks/agents/SIEM.
10. Data Tree: refs/owners/dependencies/scopes/lifecycle/verification/incidents/evidence.
11. API Tree: inventory/dependencies/plan/rotate status/verify/revoke/evidence.
12. Monetization Tree: credentials/providers/rotations/seats/enterprise/API/managed.
13. Distribution Tree: cloud/security/DevOps/MSP/OEM.
14. Automation Tree: expiry/planning/verification automatic; actual high-risk rotation protected.
15. Moat Tree: dependency graph/provider adapters/rotation reliability/outcome history.
16. Platform Tree: rotation tool→credential lifecycle OS→machine-identity infrastructure.
17. Risk Tree: secret leak/outage/orphan consumer/wrong revoke/rollback failure.
18. Scale Tree: vault→enterprise→global fleet.
19. Spinoff Tree: certificate automation/leak response; identity and permission products remain separate.
20. Command Center Dependencies: secret refs, provider registry, protected actions, health probes, incidents, audit.
21. Design-Now Requirements: every secret must have reference/owner/provider/lifecycle/dependency metadata.
22. Build-Now Requirements: extend Command Center secret registry toward safe rotation/revocation seams without exposing values.
23. Safe-to-Defer Requirements: customer discovery/provider fleet/commercial product.
24. Autonomous Mature State: expiry/dependency/rotation planning is continuous; authorized rotations execute with verification and rollback, humans handle incomplete dependency maps/emergencies.

## Saturation result
Further branches converge into agent identity, cloud permissions and runtime security already represented.

# Company 074 — Cloud Permission Optimizer

**Company ID:** `company:future:074`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:074`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-074-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no IAM policy change, privilege revocation or cloud mutation.

## Business identity
Purpose: continuously reduce excessive permissions across cloud, SaaS, databases, machine identities and agents while proving required functionality remains available.

## Product tree
IAM Inventory; Identity/Role Graph; Effective Permission Analyzer; Usage-Based Permission Evidence; Unused Privilege Detector; Privilege-Creep Monitor; Dormant Identity Detector; Least-Privilege Recommender; Policy Simulator; Blast-Radius Analyzer; Temporary Elevation; Access Request Workflow; Remediation Planner; Approved Auto-Remediation; Cross-Cloud/SaaS/DB Packs; Agent/Machine Identity Pack; Review/Audit Reports; API/SDK; Enterprise/Private Deployment.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree
Features: principal identity/type, roles/groups/policies, direct/inherited permissions, resources/scopes, last-used evidence, required operations, privilege age, risk, sensitive resources, temporary grants, simulator results, proposed delta, verification, rollback and audit.
Customers: enterprises, cloud teams, security/IAM, DevOps, MSPs, SaaS platforms and regulated organizations.
Verticals: cloud infrastructure, SaaS admin, databases, CI/CD, data platforms, AI/agent systems and enterprise apps.

## Brain capability / architecture
Brain may explain complex permission graphs and recommend least-privilege candidates. Deterministic graph/policy evaluation and provider simulation must determine effective access. Revocation requires policy, impact evidence and protected authorization.

Architecture: identity/resource graph, provider IAM adapters, policy parser/evaluator, access telemetry, risk classification, simulation, remediation plan, temporary elevation service, verification/rollback and immutable evidence.

## Agent tree
IAM Inventory Agent; Permission Graph Agent; Usage Analyst; Risk Agent; Least-Privilege Planner; Simulation Agent; Remediation Coordinator; Temporary Access Agent; Verification Agent; Audit/Compliance Agent.

## Deterministic services
Policy parsing; graph traversal; effective-permission calculation; last-used aggregation; sensitive-resource classification; proposed-policy diff; simulation; locks; change set/version; rollback; temporary expiry; evidence.

## Workflow
Inventory identities/policies/resources → calculate effective access → collect usage/required-action evidence → identify excess → simulate narrower policy → assess blast radius → recommend → protected approval → apply bounded change → verify workloads → rollback if failure → monitor drift/temporary grants → preserve audit.

## Integrations / API / data
Cloud IAM, SaaS directories, databases, Kubernetes, CI/CD, data platforms, secrets systems, identity providers, SIEM. Data: identities, policies, resources, permission graph, usage evidence, recommendations, simulations, changes and outcomes.

## Monetization / distribution
Identities/resources/accounts, cloud providers, scans, seats, enterprise/private, managed remediation and compliance packs. Distribution through cloud/security/IAM/MSP ecosystems.

## Security/privacy/compliance
Optimizer itself needs tightly scoped read access and separately authorized write access. Avoid lockouts, privilege escalation, policy confusion and cross-account mixing. Emergency access and rollback must be tested.

## Failure / edge cases
Rarely used permissions, disaster-recovery permissions, service account without telemetry, inherited wildcards, deny overrides, resource policy vs identity policy, organization policy, provider semantics, temporary incident access, application burst after months idle. Absence of observed use is not proof of safe removal.

## Scale / overlap
Cloud account → enterprise identity graph → cross-cloud least-privilege platform. Overlap #75 access review, #58 employee lifecycle, #73 secrets, #91 agent identity. #074 owns effective permission optimization.

## Classification
**DESIGN NOW:** explicit scopes/resources, permission provenance, temporary expiry, simulation/dry-run, reversible policy changes and identity graph.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center authorization/Agency delegation should already enforce subset-only authority and expiry; reverse-map strengthens simulation/explainability needs.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** provider policy parsers, usage telemetry and remediation simulator.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** cloud/SaaS connectors/customer policies/UI.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** organization-wide cross-cloud permission graph.

# Company 075 — Identity Access Review Autopilot

**Company ID:** `company:future:075`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:075`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-075-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no access revocation, attestation submission or account mutation.

## Business identity
Purpose: automate recurring certification of human, contractor, vendor, service-account and AI-agent access across apps, cloud, databases, groups and privileged roles.

## Product tree
Access Inventory; Review Campaigns; Continuous Certification; Manager/Owner Attestation; Risk-Based Review; Dormant Account Review; Privileged Access Review; Service/Machine/Agent Identity Review; Application/Group/Role Review; Evidence Collector; Exception/Justification; Revocation Workflow; Reviewer Delegation; Review Escalation; Compliance Reports; API/SDK; Enterprise/Private Deployment; Framework/Industry Packs.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree
Features: subject identity/type/status, manager/owner, resource/app, role/group/permission, source of grant, last use, privilege/risk, review period, reviewer, decision, justification, exception/expiry, revocation state, evidence and audit.
Customers: enterprises, security/IAM/GRC teams, MSPs, regulated organizations and SaaS/platform operators.
Verticals: cloud/SaaS, finance-adjacent, healthcare admin, government, education, technology, data platforms and agentic systems.

## Brain capability / architecture
Brain may summarize why access exists, flag anomalous grants and recommend review priority. Deterministic identity/access data and policy drive certification. Brain cannot auto-attest that access is appropriate when evidence is insufficient.

Architecture: identity/resource/access graph, HR/vendor/machine lifecycle feeds, review campaign engine, risk rules, usage evidence, reviewer/ownership graph, decision/exception ledger, revocation adapter and compliance evidence.

## Agent tree
Access Inventory Agent; Campaign Planner; Ownership Resolver; Risk Reviewer; Dormant Access Agent; Privileged Access Agent; Machine/Agent Identity Reviewer; Evidence Agent; Exception Agent; Revocation Coordinator; Compliance Report Agent; QA Agent.

## Deterministic services
Access graph; campaign scheduler; reviewer assignment; due/escalation; last-use ingestion; risk flags; attestation state; exception expiry; idempotent revocation request; reconciliation; immutable evidence.

## Workflow
Snapshot current access → resolve identity/resource ownership → select campaign/risk scope → assign reviewers → present access + usage/provenance → retain/revoke/exception decision → require justification for risky retains → protected revocation workflow → verify downstream removal → reconcile unresolved items → close campaign with audit evidence; continuous mode opens targeted reviews on material change.

## Integrations / API / data
IdP/IAM, HRIS, vendor systems, cloud, SaaS directories, databases, PAM, agent identity registry, SIEM/GRC/ticketing. Data: identities, access grants, resources, ownership, usage, campaigns, reviews, exceptions, revocations and evidence.

## Monetization / distribution
Identities/apps/resources, review campaigns, seats, enterprise/private, compliance packs, API and managed certification. Distribution through IAM/GRC/security/MSP ecosystems.

## Security/privacy/compliance
Review data is security-sensitive. Least privilege, reviewer authorization, no cross-tenant views, decision provenance, tamper evidence and protected revocation. Avoid rubber-stamp AI recommendations; uncertain ownership/risk must remain visible.

## Failure / edge cases
Manager departed, orphaned service account, shared account, emergency access, nested groups, conflicting role owners, rarely used DR access, acquired company, contractor extended, account disabled but group persists, revocation fails downstream. Review completion requires reconciliation, not just reviewer clicks.

## Scale / overlap
Periodic spreadsheet review → continuous enterprise certification → identity governance service. Overlap #58 employee lifecycle, #74 permission optimization, #91 agent identity. #075 owns review/attestation lifecycle.

## Classification
**DESIGN NOW:** identity/resource ownership, access provenance, decision/exception expiry, revocation reconciliation and evidence.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center own device/session/agent/provider authorization should remain reviewable and owner-visible; reverse-map supports a generalized access inventory.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** enterprise access graph/connectors/campaign engine.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** customer IAM/GRC packs/UI/pricing.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** continuous global identity certification graph.

13. Distribution Tree: IAM/GRC/security/MSP/OEM.
14. Automation Tree: inventory/risk/campaign/reconciliation automatic; attestation/revocation gated by policy.
15. Moat Tree: access/ownership graph, review outcomes, connectors, risk heuristics.
16. Platform Tree: review tool→continuous certification→identity-governance layer.
17. Risk Tree: wrong reviewer/rubber-stamp/lockout/stale access/failed revoke/privacy leak.
18. Scale Tree: campaign→enterprise continuous→global identity graph.
